initial_response.goal: Litho-Density log의 Pe와 bulk-density 측정값이 각각 무엇에 더 민감한지 내부 자료로 구분해줘.
initial_response.final_answer:
Bulk-density 측정값은 주로 암석의 다공성(porosity)에 더 민감하다. [KB1]
Bulk-density 측정값은 암석의 다공성에 민감하지만, 암석의 구성 성분과 암석 내 유체의 영향을 받을 수 있다. [KB1] [KB4]
Bulk-density 측정값은 암석의 다공성에 더 민감하지만, 암석의 구성 성분과 유체의 영향을 받을 수 있으며, 이는 암석의 성분에 따라 달라질 수 있다. [KB1] [KB4]

criteria.reason: Pe 측정값은 암석의 구성 성분(암석의 종류, 즉 라이트로지)에 더 민감하다는 점이 KB1에서 명시되어 있음. Pe 측정값은 주로 암석의 구성 성분에 반응하고, 부수적으로 다공성과 유체에 영향을 받는다고 명시되어 있음. 이는 Pe 측정값이 특정 지질학적 매개변수(암석의 종류)에 더 민감한지를 평가하기 위한 데이터 분석 기준을 충족함. [KB1].

Bulk-density 측정값은 주로 암석의 다공성에 민감하다는 점이 KB1에서 명시되어 있음. Bulk-density 측정값은 주로 다공성에 반응하고, 부수적으로 암석의 구성 성분과 유체에 영향을 받는다고 명시되어 있음. 이는 Bulk-density 측정값이 특정 지질학적 매개변수(다공성)에 더 민감한지를 평가하기 위한 데이터 분석 기준을 충족함. [KB1].
Pe 측정값은 암석의 구성 성분에 더 민감하고, Bulk-density 측정값은 암석의 다공성에 더 민감하다는 점이 KB1에서 명시되어 있음. 이는 Pe와 Bulk-density 측정값의 민감도를 비교하기 위한 통계적 기준을 충족함. [KB1].

5.3 The Litho Density Tools
The Litho-Density* Log is an improved and expanded version of the FDC log.  In 
addition to the bulk density measurement, the tool also measures the photoelectric 
absorption index of the formation, Pe.  Photoelectric absorption can be related to 
lithology;  whereas the  ρb measurement responds primarily to porosity and secondarily 
to rock matrix and pore fluid, the Pe measurement responds primarily to rock matrix 
(lithology) and secondarily to porosity and pore fluid.

In  known  lithology,  the  grain  density,  ρma,  can  be  chosen  from  a  table  like  Table  3D.5.
Sensitivity  can  be  analyzed  directly  by  taking  the  partial  derivative  of  the  response  equation
with respect to grain density. For a 30-p.u., water-filled sandstone, an error of 0.05 g/cm3 in
the supposed grain density will only alter the calculated porosity by 2 p.u. A similar analysis
of  the  sensitivity  to  fluid  density  shows  that  a  variation  of  more  than  0.1  g/cm3  in  the  fluid
density corresponds to a similar 2-p.u. error in the calculated porosity.
This  is  fortunate  because  fluid  density  within  the  density  tool’s  volume  of  investigation
may be very difficult to estimate. As already discussed, because of its shallow depth of investi-

may be taken to be that of the mud filtrate. The eff

gation,  the  density  log  is  commonly  a  flushed-zone  device,  and  the  fluid  density  that  it  sees
may be taken to be that of the mud filtrate. The effect of a small amount of immovable hydro-
carbon or connate water can, more often than not, be ignored. If gas is present, its low density
will produce an apparent increase in porosity. Here, we could have a case in which, to calcu-
late density porosity, we must first know the average flushed-zone fluid saturation.
As  discussed  in  the  section  about  radiation  transport,  the  biggest  hitch  in  gamma-gamma
scattering density evaluation is the difference between bulk density and electron density. The
device measures electron density. As Table 3D.5 shows, this matters only for fluids. Knowing
that  the  tool  will  be  used  in  fluid-filled  rocks,  the  service  companies  transform  the  electron
density  to  a  water-filled,  porous  limestone,  calibrated  bulk  density.  The  apparent  density  as
read by the tool is thus altered to read:
ρb_log = 1.0704ρe −0.188. .................................................. (3D.28)

investigated by the tool differs appreciably from that of water.  In particular, light 
hydrocarbons (gas) can significantly influence the response of all three porosity logs.
Even the nature of type of pore structure affects the tool response.  The neutron and 
density logs respond to total porosity - that is, the sum of the primary (intergranular 
or intercrystalline) porosity and the secondary (vugs, fissures, fractures) porosity.  The 
sonic logs, however, tend to respond only to evenly distributed primary porosity.
To determine porosity when any of these complicating situations exists requires more 
data than provided by a single porosity log.  Fortunately, neutron, density, and sonic 
logs respond differently to matrix minerals, to the presence of gas or light oils, and 
to the geometry of pore structure.  Combinations of these logs and the photoelectric 
cross section index, Pe, measurement from the Litho-Density* log and the thorium, 
uranium, and potassium measurement from the NGS* natural gamma ray spectrometry 
log can be used to unravel complex matrix or fluid mixtures and thereby provide a 
more accurate  porosity determination.
